title: Being followed
text: The same gray sedan has been parked across the street for three days.

outcomes.text: I stayed in, stayed quiet. The sedan disappeared.
I went quiet for four months and they simply waited me out. The sedan was there the week I came back.
It was a detective. Now they know I know.
It was a private investigator hired by my ex. Awkward.
{cop.first} made a call. The sedan was gone the next day.
{cop.first} asked why I wanted to know, and I could hear {cop.him} deciding something about me.

title: Informant
text: An old associate got arrested and is offering to testify against you.

outcomes.text: They got a good lawyer and kept their mouth shut.
I paid for the lawyer, and the lawyer advised them that cooperating was the better deal.
I disappeared for a few months. The case went cold.
I left town, and leaving town was the detail that made them certain it had been me.
They talked.
They didn't know as much as they thought.

title: A shady offer
text: {s.first}, a friend of a friend, says {s.he} can get you anything. Anything at all.

outcomes.text: {s.first} gave me an address. The Black Market is open to me now.
{s.first} gave me an address and made a point of taking my number as well, which I had not offered.
I walked away. I don't need that kind of trouble.
I walked away, and {s.first} told the friend of a friend that I was not to be trusted with anything.

choices.label: Ask what {s.first} wants out of it

outcomes.text: {s.first} wanted a name, not money. I gave {s.him} one and got the address for free.
Asking was the wrong move. {s.first} decided I was police and the friend of a friend stopped calling.

title: Sharp eyes
text: At a party, a jeweler looks closely at your watch and smirks.

outcomes.text: "It's a fake? No way." Everyone laughed. I didn't.
I laughed first and loudest and turned it into the story of the evening. Nobody remembered it as a humiliation.
I insisted. The jeweler dropped it, but word got around.
I insisted, and he offered to open the back of it there and then in front of everybody.

choices.label: Ask him what a real one is worth

outcomes.text: He told me, and then told me where the fake had been made, which was more interesting than the watch.
He told me what the real one costs, loudly, and then what mine was worth, more loudly.

title: Recognized
text: A guest at your house recognizes a painting on your wall. It was in the news. It was stolen.

outcomes.text: They bought it. I moved the painting to the basement.
They said they believed me and photographed it on the way out.
They took the money. I hope.
They took the money, and came back for more of it every year after that.
They called the police.
They said nothing at all, to me or to anybody. I never worked out why.

title: Exotic pet
text: Your exotic pet {x.first} got out and is sitting on the neighbor's car.

outcomes.text: It worked. The neighbor has moved out.
The meat worked on {x.first} and not on the neighbour, who had already been on the phone for ten minutes.
Animal control confiscated {x.first} and fined me $10,000.
Animal control came, and the officer who arrived had wanted one of these {x.his} whole life and quietly wrote it up as a stray.
{x.first} now lives in a proper enclosure at my zoo.
{x.first} went to the zoo and never settled. Some animals know the difference between a big cage and outside.

title: Forger arrested
text: The forger who made your documents was arrested. Police have his client list.

outcomes.text: I booked the next flight out.
I used it, and it worked perfectly, which means it is still out there working for somebody.
I burned the passport in the sink.
I burned it, and a fortnight later needed exactly the thing I had burned.
They came knocking.
Nobody came. My name must not have been in the book.

title: Market sweep
text: Police are sweeping the street market where you sell knockoffs.

outcomes.text: I got away with half my stock.
I tripped over a table of handbags. Arrested.
I bought a scarf from the stall next to mine. Nobody looked twice.
I played the shopper right up until an officer asked me to open the bag I was carrying.

choices.label: Give the stock away to the crowd

outcomes.text: I emptied the table into a hundred pairs of hands in about forty seconds. There was nothing left to seize.
I gave it away, and three of the people I gave it to were stopped at the end of the street with it.

title: Clean slate
text: It's been a quiet year. Maybe it's time to go straight for good.

outcomes.text: I cut ties with the old crowd.
I went straight, and the old crowd took that as a statement about them, and behaved accordingly.
Old habits die hard.
One more score turned out to be a much bigger one than advertised, and a much worse one.

choices.label: Go straight, and give back what you can

outcomes.text: I paid back everybody I could find. It cost most of what I had and it is the only thing I am proud of.
Paying people back meant contacting them, and two of them took that as an admission and used it.

title: Lost in the woods
text: On a hike, you realize you haven't seen a trail marker in an hour.

outcomes.text: The stream led to a road. I hitchhiked home.
The stream led nowhere. Search and rescue found me two days later.
A ranger found me at dusk.
I stayed put for two nights. They found me on the third morning about four hundred metres from a road.
One bar at the top of the ridge was all it took. They picked me up in ninety minutes.
I climbed for an hour, got no signal, and could no longer find the way I had come up.

title: Bear!
text: A black bear is standing on the trail, twenty feet away.

outcomes.text: It stared, then lumbered off. My legs didn't stop shaking for an hour.
I made myself big and it decided to make itself bigger. I got down the trail on adrenaline and a badly turned ankle.
Never run from a bear. It chased me. I survived, barely.
I ran, which was the wrong thing, and it did not follow, which was pure luck and I know it.
The photo won a local wildlife contest.
I got the phone up and it came four steps closer, and the photograph is of nothing but blur and grass.

title: Fishing tournament
text: There's a fishing tournament at the lake this weekend. $5,000 prize.

outcomes.text: I watched and ate a hot dog. A good day.
I watched from the dock and the man who won told me afterwards I should have entered. He was right.

choices.label: Enter, and fish where nobody else is

outcomes.text: Everybody crowded the inlet. I went to the far bank and took second place and a thousand dollars.
There was a reason nobody was fishing the far bank. I caught weed for six hours.

title: Family trip
text: {k.first} begs you to take {k.him} camping.

outcomes.text: We roasted marshmallows and counted shooting stars. {k.first} will remember this forever.
It rained for three days and the tent leaked and {k.first} talks about that trip more than any other.
{k.first} was crushed.
I said I was too busy, and {k.first} said it was fine, and stopped asking after that.

choices.label: Go, but take the whole family

outcomes.text: All of us in two tents. It was chaos and it is the trip everybody still talks about.
All of us in two tents, and by the second night it was clear {k.first} had wanted it to be just the two of us.

title: Old map
text: You found an old hand-drawn map in a secondhand book about the local caves.

outcomes.text: At the end of the map: a rusted box of old coins.
At the end of the map: a note reading "made you look."
A collector paid $300 for it.
The collector paid three hundred, and there was a piece in the paper eight months later about what he found.

choices.label: Give it to the local museum

outcomes.text: The curator went very quiet and then very excited. There is a case with my name on the card.
The museum took it, filed it, and I have never once seen it on display.

title: Injured hawk
text: You find a hawk with a broken wing by the trail.

choices.label: Take it to a rehab center

outcomes.text: They saved it. They let me release it myself a month later.
They tried for three weeks. The wing had been broken too long before I found it.
The hawk joined the rescue wing at my zoo.
The hawk went to my zoo and is the only bird there the keepers will not go near.
I left it. I thought about it for days.
I left it, and walked the same trail a week later, and it was still there.

title: Dirt race
text: A local motocross race needs one more rider.

outcomes.text: I finished on the podium!
I ate dirt on the first corner. Broken wrist.
I cheered from the fence and got covered in mud.
I watched, and one of the riders went into the barrier at the second corner, and nobody cheered after that.
I borrowed a bike I had never sat on and came fourth, which I have decided counts as winning.
I borrowed a bike I did not know and put it into a fence, and had to pay for the fence and the bike.

title: Something fell
text: A streak of light crossed the sky and landed in the field behind your house.

outcomes.text: A real meteorite! Still warm.
I found the crater and a lump of somebody's satellite, which a very serious man came to collect the next day.
The next day, a neighbor was on the news with a meteorite.
I stayed in, and it turned out to be a transformer fire that took out half the field.
I rang the university. Two of them drove out that night and let me keep a piece of it.
I rang the university and they sent somebody the following Tuesday, by which point half the field had been dug over.

title: Friendly checkup
text: {d.first}, who works as a doctor, notices you look pale at dinner.

outcomes.text: {d.first} caught something early. It could have been serious.
{d.first} looked me over at the table, said it was nothing, and I have never been sure {d.he} looked properly.
I told {d.first} I'm fine. I'm probably fine.
I brushed it off, and {d.first} quietly rang a fortnight later to ask if I had seen anybody about it. {d.He} had not been asking idly.
I booked a real appointment instead of asking over dinner. {d.first} said that was the most sensible thing I had ever done.
I booked properly, waited eleven weeks, and by then whatever it was had gone.

title: Fine print
text: You're about to sign a big contract. {lw.first} offers to read it first.

outcomes.text: {lw.first} found a clause that would have cost me everything.
{lw.first} read it, found nothing, and the thing that went wrong two years later was in the part neither of us thought mattered.
I signed it. It was fine. Probably.
I signed without reading, and clause eleven cost me a great deal more than a favour would have.
I insisted on paying. {lw.first} read it like a paying client's contract, which is to say twice.
Paying turned a friend into a supplier, and it has been slightly formal between us ever since.

title: Car trouble
text: Your car is making a horrible grinding noise. {mc.first} is a mechanic.

outcomes.text: {mc.first} fixed it in an afternoon for the cost of a pizza.
{mc.first} fixed it and it went again a month later, and now neither of us knows how to raise it.
The garage charged me $1,800.
The garage charged eighteen hundred and did it properly, and {mc.first} heard I had not asked.
We did it together in {mc.his} garage on a Sunday. I can do it myself now and we do this most months.
{mc.first} showed me, and I understood none of it, and we both pretended otherwise.

title: The scoop
text: {jr.first}, a journalist, is working on a story that mentions you.

outcomes.text: {jr.first}'s piece was glowing.
I gave {jr.first} everything and {jr.he} wrote the piece {jr.he} had already decided to write.
{jr.first} cut my name out.
{jr.first} refused. Journalistic integrity.
I handed {jr.first} something more interesting than me, and {jr.he} took it, and the piece about me never ran.
{jr.first} took the better story and ran both.

title: Insider tip
text: {b.first}, who works at a bank, hints that a big merger is coming.

outcomes.text: The merger went through. I made $40,000.
The SEC noticed the timing.
{b.first} looked relieved.
I told {b.first} I had not heard it, and watched the merger go through, and did the arithmetic anyway.
I reported the conversation. {b.first} lost {b.his} job, and the regulator wrote to thank me.
I reported it and nothing whatever happened, except that {b.first} found out who had.

title: A favor
text: {cop.first}, a police officer, asks you to keep an eye on a neighbor they suspect.

outcomes.text: My tip led to an arrest. {cop.first} owes me one.
I watched for a month and there was nothing to see. I had been spying on a man who fed birds.
I stayed out of it.
I stayed out of it, and what the neighbour was actually doing came out eighteen months later.
I told him he was being watched. Whatever he had been doing, he stopped, and nobody was arrested.
I warned him, and he thanked me, and moved what he had been keeping to a house two streets over.

title: Industry intro
text: {pr.first}, a film producer, invites you to a party full of industry people.

outcomes.text: I met a casting director who asked for my number.
I spilled wine on a studio head. Memorable, at least.
I stayed home.
I stayed home, and {pr.first} stopped inviting me to things, which is how that works.
I went and talked to nobody important and had an excellent evening, and got a call the following week anyway.
I went with no agenda, and spent four hours watching a room full of people who all had one.

title: Off-market
text: {re.first}, a real estate agent, knows about a house being sold below value.

outcomes.text: I bought it for a steal and rented it out.
It was below value for a reason that was under the floor and cost more to fix than the discount.
I passed. Someone else got a bargain.
I passed, and the buyer spent two years and a fortune discovering what was wrong with it.
The survey came back clean and I bought it knowing exactly what I was buying.
The survey took nine days and somebody else bought it on the fourth.

title: Tutoring
text: {t.first}, who's a teacher, offers to tutor {k.first} for free.

outcomes.text: {k.first}'s grades went way up.
{t.first} tutored {k.first} for a term and the two of them got on so well that {k.first} now wants to teach.
I paid the going rate. {t.first} took it, and worked {k.first} much harder than a favour would have.
{t.first} was offended by the offer and the tutoring quietly did not happen.
{k.first} wanted to manage it alone, and did, and I am glad I listened.
I turned it down on {k.first}'s behalf without asking {k.him}, which {k.he} found out about.

title: Dinner party
text: {ch.first}, who's a chef, offers to cater your party.

outcomes.text: People are still talking about the food.
{ch.first} cooked for forty people for nothing and I did not think, until afterwards, about what I had asked for.
Pizza is also good.
I ordered pizza with a chef in the room, which {ch.first} found much funnier than I had feared.
I cooked for twenty with a chef in the room and {ch.first} said two things that made all of it work.
I cooked it myself in front of a professional, which is a thing I will not be doing again.

title: Buddy pass
text: {pl.first} is a pilot and can get you a cheap flight anywhere.

outcomes.text: I flew to the other side of the world for $80.
Standby is standby. I spent two days in an airport and flew home without leaving the terminal.
Maybe later.
I said maybe later for four years, and then {pl.first} changed airlines.
Two buddy passes and a week on the other side of the world with the person I most wanted to see it with.
Two standby seats never came up together. One of us flew and it was not me.

title: Fire!
text: A fire broke out in your kitchen. {ff.first} happened to be visiting.

outcomes.text: {ff.first} put it out in seconds with a towel and a lid.
{ff.first} put it out and then walked me round the house pointing at everything else that was going to happen one day.
Lid on, gas off, done, with a professional watching. {ff.first} said I would have been fine either way.
I threw water on a pan fire with a firefighter three metres away, and {ff.first} has never let it go.

choices.label: Get everyone out and call it in

outcomes.text: {ff.first} got everyone onto the drive first and the brigade did the rest. The kitchen is gone and nobody is hurt.
We got out, and it was a pan fire that would have gone out under a lid, and the brigade were extremely nice about it.

title: Working for you
text: {e.first}, who works at {biz}, invited the whole team to {e.his} house for a barbecue.

outcomes.text: It was a great night. The team feels like a family.
I went, stayed too long, and heard three things about my own company that nobody would have said at work.
I skipped it. The boss shouldn't hang out with staff.
I skipped it, and the photos went up on Monday, and I was the only person in the office not in any of them.

choices.label: Go for an hour and pay for the food

outcomes.text: I turned up, paid for the lot, and left before anybody had to watch what they were saying.
Paying for it made it a work event, which is precisely what it had not been until I arrived.

title: Home from deployment
text: {s.first} is home from a military deployment.

outcomes.text: {s.first} teared up when {s.he} saw everyone.
I filled a room with people and noise, and {s.first} lasted twenty minutes before going and sitting in the car.
We talked for an hour.
I just called, and it was the right call. {s.first} said the last thing {s.he} wanted was a room full of people.
{s.first} wanted a quiet pint and no questions. That is what we did, every week, for a year.
I asked, and {s.first} said {s.he} did not know, and neither of us knew what to do with that.

title: Name on the door
text: Your old sports fame could sell gym memberships.

outcomes.text: Head to Occupation → Business. Your past career gives you an edge in fitness.
I put my name on a door. It turns out a name gets people through it once and nothing else.
No chain, no name on a door. One gym, one squad, and four of them went further than I did.
I coached for two seasons and could not stand watching people do badly the thing I used to do well.
I said no. It was my name before it was worth anything and I would like it back.
I turned it down, and somebody opened a chain two years later with a name close enough to sue over and not close enough to win.

title: Own your masters
text: Your old label still owns your songs. You could start your own.

outcomes.text: I'm going to build my own label. Occupation → Business.
I looked into buying my masters back first. The number they quoted is the reason I am starting a label.
I recorded the whole catalogue again, older and better, and told everybody which version to buy.
I re-recorded it all and nobody wanted the new versions. The originals are the originals.
They own the songs. They do not own what it was like to write them.
I let it go, and then heard one of them in an advert for something I would never have agreed to.

title: True believers
text: Your old campaign volunteers still send you letters. They'd follow you anywhere.

outcomes.text: I'm thinking about starting something bigger than a campaign. Activities → Social → Cult.
I wrote to all of them at once, and four hundred people replied within a week.
I wrote back thanking them.
I wrote back politely, and the letters kept coming for eleven years, and I answered every one.

choices.label: Put them to work on something real

outcomes.text: I pointed four hundred true believers at a housing campaign. They won it in eleven months.
I gave them a cause and they wanted a leader, and kept coming back to ask what I thought about everything.

title: The boss's tiger
text: The Don is going to prison and needs someone to take care of his tiger.

choices.label: Take the tiger to your zoo

outcomes.text: The tiger is now the star of my zoo. Nobody asks where it came from.
The tiger came with paperwork that did not survive contact with an inspector.
The Don won't forget this.
I refused, and the tiger went somewhere much worse, and I hear about it occasionally.

choices.label: Take it, and report where it came from

outcomes.text: I took the tiger and told the authorities exactly where it had come from. The paperwork is clean and so is the enclosure.
I took it and reported it, and the Don found out which of those two things I had done.

title: Security consulting
text: Your old intelligence contacts want to hire a private firm for off-the-books work.

outcomes.text: I made $200,000 for a week of work I can't talk about.
The week of work went wrong in a country I had not been told I was going to.
I'm out. For real this time.
I stayed retired, and they took it well, and asked again every eighteen months for the rest of my life.

choices.label: Take it, but only the legal part

outcomes.text: I did the risk assessments and none of the rest. Less money, no nights awake.
I took the clean half and found out afterwards what the clean half had been used to plan.

title: Superfans
text: Your fans have started a Discord that is getting a little... worshipful.

outcomes.text: I'm going to give them something to believe in. Activities → Social → Cult.
I leaned in, and within a month it had rules I had not written and a hierarchy I did not choose.
They calmed down. Mostly.
I asked them to calm down, and they decided that asking was itself a message, and read it very closely.
I asked them to raise money instead of worship. They raised an amount that embarrassed me.
They raised the money and then wanted to know what I would like them to do next, and next, and next.
